WPSS No.815 of 2023
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Vipin Singh and Mr. Kapil 
Prasad Gaur, Advocates for the 
petitioner. 
Mr. Pooran Singh Rawat, 
Additional Chief Standing Counsel 
for the State.
Mr. Ashish Joshi and Mr. 
C.K. Sharma, Advocates for the 
Public Service Commission. 
The candidature of the 
petitioner has been rejected for his 
appointment as a Police Constable.
It is the case of the petitioner 
that his rejection is not as per law. 
He belongs to the hill category; he 
meets all the physical requirement 
for recruitment.
On behalf of the respondents 
it is being stated that the petitioner 
did not place for perusal of the 
Public Service Commission (“the 
Commission”) his documents that 
he belongs to the hill category. 
But, the question is, whether 
the Commission ever asked for 
such documents? If so, whether 
the Commission ever made any 
communication in writing? 
Whether the Commission before 
rejection of candidature of the 
petitioner required him to produce 
such documents revealing the  consequences in non-production of 
it? When questioned, learned 
counsel for the Commission seeks 
time. 
List on 06.06.2023, just after 
fresh cases. 
 
(Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 05.06.2023
Sanjay

WPSS No.815 of 2023
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Vipin Singh and Mr. Kapil 
Prasad Gaur, Advocates for the 
petitioner.
Mr. Pooran Singh Bisht, 
Additional Chief Standing Counsel 
for the State/respondent nos.1 and 
2. 
Mr. C.K. Sharma, Advocate for 
the Uttarakhand Subordinate 
Service Selection 
Commission/respondent no.3.
Mr. Alok Mehra and Mr. 
Ashish Joshi, Advocates for the 
Uttarakhand Public Service 
Commission/respondent no.4.
Heard learned counsel for the 
parties and perused the record.
Admit.
The petitioner applied for the 
position of Constable in 
Uttarakhand Police or PAC/IRB, 
etc. He cleared the examination, 
but finally his candidature was 
rejected on the ground that he did 
not produce his certificate that he 
belongs to the hill category. 
Learned counsel for the 
petitioner would submit that, in 
fact, the petitioner had the 
certificate, but he did not produce 
it on time and for that ground, he 
could have been given an  opportunity to produce it and his 
candidature could not have been 
rejected. 
When the matter was taken 
up yesterday, the Court wanted to 
know, as the whether the 
Commission ever asked for such 
documents? If so, whether the 
Commission ever made any 
communication in writing? 
Whether the Commission before 
rejection of candidature of the 
petitioner required him to produce 
such documents revealing the 
consequences in non-production of 
it?
Learned counsel for the 
respondent no.4, Uttarakhand 
Public Service Commission today, 
under instruction, gives a 
statement that any such 
communication was not made. 
Having heard, this Court is of 
the view that this matter requires 
deliberation. 
Admit.
Learned Additional Chief 
Standing Counsel takes notice on 
behalf of respondent nos.1 and 2. 
Mr. C.K. Sharma, Advocate 
takes notice on behalf of 
respondent no.3. Mr. Alok Mehra, Advocate 
takes notice on behalf of 
respondent no.4.
Counter affidavit may be filed 
within four weeks.
Two weeks thereafter, 
rejoinder affidavit, if any, may be 
filed. 
List this case on 12.09.2023.
Heard on Interim Relief 
Application (IA) No.1 of 2023.
It is argued that the 
appointment letters have already 
been issued by the respondent 
authorities and the joining would 
be done from tomorrow onwards. It 
would be the process which were 
initiated by virtue of an 
advertisement dated 28.12.2021. 
Since challenge is made to a 
selection process, at this stage, the 
Court can only observe that the 
selection that has been done 
pursuant to the advertisement 
shall remain subject to the 
decision of this writ petition. 
Interim relief application 
stands disposed of accordingly. 
(Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 06.06.2023
Sanjay
